[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">AgentTranscriptMaterializer</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/AgentTranscriptMaterializer/#L55)

Turns every agent transcript under `dev_docs/agents/transcripts/` into a loadable Field **document** — a `<out>/<name>/metadata.edn` scene an editor/welcome can open, run and edit. This is how the transcript corpus becomes both the docs gallery workspace and the welcome "starting points": one source of truth (the yaml), documents derived at build time.

## BoxCodeCompileGuard.kt { #boxcodecompileguard-kt }

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/examples/BoxCodeCompileGuard.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/BoxCodeCompileGuard/)

### BoxCodeCompileGuard { #boxcodecompileguard-kt-boxcodecompileguard }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">BoxCodeCompileGuard</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/BoxCodeCompileGuard/#L23)

The landing guard that box code still compiles: each named transcript goes down the path [`DemoTranscriptExecSmokeTest`](examples.md#demotranscriptexecsmoketest-kt-demotranscriptexecsmoketest) classifies it for. COMPILE_ONLY transcripts (the ones that would open a window) build their graph and compile with evaluation skipped; EXECUTE transcripts are headless-safe and run, because a later box may need what an earlier one defines when evaluated; KOTLINJS transcripts compile through the Kotlin/JS path.

### ClothSimulationExample { #clothsimulationexample-kt-clothsimulationexample }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">ClothSimulationExample</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/ClothSimulationExample/#L16)

Demo of [`Cloth`](simulation.md#cloth-kt-cloth) — the reusable grid-cloth builder over `SimdVerlet`'s 4-slot distance constraints. All of the physics lives in [`Cloth`](simulation.md#cloth-kt-cloth) now; what is left here is the part that is genuinely example-shaped: standing up a simulation, wrapping the frame loop so the grabbed particle gets a red crosshair, and the process-level "most recent simulation" handle that lets an interactive box call [`grabNearest`](examples.md#clothsimulationexample-kt--clothsimulationexample--grabnearest) without holding one.

## CodeUseTelemetryBusyRecoverySmokeTest.kt { #codeusetelemetrybusyrecoverysmoketest-kt }

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/examples/CodeUseTelemetryBusyRecoverySmokeTest.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/CodeUseTelemetryBusyRecoverySmokeTest/)

### CodeUseTelemetryBusyRecoverySmokeTest { #codeusetelemetrybusyrecoverysmoketest-kt-codeusetelemetrybusyrecoverysmoketest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">CodeUseTelemetryBusyRecoverySmokeTest</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/CodeUseTelemetryBusyRecoverySmokeTest/#L26)

A second connection holds the telemetry database's write lock through two of the writer's 5 s busy timeouts. The writer must stay enabled, report the SQLITE_BUSY retries and the events it is holding, and commit every one of them once the lock is released. Analysis of a held compile event must wait for that commit.

## DocumentToTranscript.kt { #documenttotranscript-kt }

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/examples/DocumentToTranscript.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/DocumentToTranscript/)

### DocumentToTranscript { #documenttotranscript-kt-documenttotranscript }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">DocumentToTranscript</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/DocumentToTranscript/#L53)

Writes an OperationTranscript yaml from a saved Field document — the reverse of [`AgentTranscriptMaterializer`](examples.md#agenttranscriptmaterializer-kt-agenttranscriptmaterializer). It is how a document built by hand, or a nightly demo under `dev_docs/agents/demos/`, becomes a transcript in `dev_docs/agents/transcripts/` without anyone retyping its boxes: the document is what the boxes currently contain, so the transcript is generated from it, never paraphrased.

## KotlinToJsSpikeTest.kt { #kotlintojsspiketest-kt }

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/examples/KotlinToJsSpikeTest.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/KotlinToJsSpikeTest/)

### KotlinToJsSpikeTest { #kotlintojsspiketest-kt-kotlintojsspiketest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">KotlinToJsSpikeTest</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/KotlinToJsSpikeTest/#L30)

Proves the Kotlin->JS RemoteJS seam end to end, in-process from a Field JVM: 1. A self-contained Kotlin snippet that uses `operator fun plus` (the thing ASTA exists to fake in raw JS) compiles to a single plain-module JS string via [`KotlinToJsCompiler`](languages.md#kotlintojscompiler-kt-kotlintojscompiler). 2. A deliberately broken snippet surfaces a structured compile diagnostic (line + message), i.e. errors are catchable at the Kotlin source before the browser ever runs anything. 3. If `node` is on PATH, the produced JS is actually executed and its output verified — proving the module is directly eval-able (which is what the head's `global.eval(code)` needs).

| Declaration | Summary |

| <a id="kotlintojsspiketest-kt--kotlintojsspiketest--main"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">args</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Array</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/KotlinToJsSpikeTest/#L33) |  |

## RectslBoxToolsSmokeTest.kt { #rectslboxtoolssmoketest-kt }

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/examples/ai/RectslBoxToolsSmokeTest.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/ai/RectslBoxToolsSmokeTest/)

### RectslBoxToolsSmokeTest { #rectslboxtoolssmoketest-kt-rectslboxtoolssmoketest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">RectslBoxToolsSmokeTest</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/ai/RectslBoxToolsSmokeTest/#L51)

Step-2 slice for box-authored AI tools: the RectSL studio tool set + the image-return and box-state-escape primitives. Drives the REAL box path — a box whose `code` declares a ki-var and calls `registerRectslStudioTools()` (unqualified, via the intro import) — then asserts, without a live model and without requiring a GPU: - `rectsl.check` compiles good source and reports diagnostics for bad source; - a `{{ … }}` escape compiled against the box's engine reads the box's live ki-var (the "escapes reference box state" requirement) — prewarmed off the runloop, then invoked; - the image-return primitive marshals correctly (base64 kept out of the JSON output); - `rectsl.run` fails gracefully (a structured tool error) when no renderer is in context — the GPU happy-path reuses the gallery-proven RectSLRenderRunner and runs in a live document.

| Declaration | Summary |

## OpenDlssNrTeardownSmoke.kt { #opendlssnrteardownsmoke-kt }

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/examples/four/OpenDlssNrTeardownSmoke.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/four/OpenDlssNrTeardownSmoke/)

### OpenDlssNrTeardownSmoke { #opendlssnrteardownsmoke-kt-opendlssnrteardownsmoke }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">OpenDlssNrTeardownSmoke</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/four/OpenDlssNrTeardownSmoke/#L41)

The renderer goes away while an [`OpenDlssNrStudy`](graphics.md#opendlssnrstudy-kt-opendlssnrstudy) is still open on it, which is what quitting or disposing the graphics context does to a box that was never stopped. The study is closed by the renderer, before its device, and the box's own later close is harmless. Without the native library the study runs in source mode, so this needs a GPU but not NVIDIA.

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">ShaderReloadTransitionSmoke</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/four/ShaderReloadTransitionSmoke/#L59)

The reload-transition matrix, on a real device: one box, one graphics module, and a full reload (`reloadShader`) per row, with frames rendered between them so buffers are written and retirements go through the renderer's deferred queue. ## slideshow_example.kt { #slideshow-example-kt }

Example slideshows demonstrating the slideshow DSL

To use these, create boxes in Field and run the code in one of them.
The slideshow will guide users through the document.

NEW FEATURES:
- Custom link callbacks: Links can execute Kotlin code via #custom:callbackName
- Template system: Use {{propertyName}} to reference box properties/variables
- Shared chat: Use withChat(id = "templateId") to share chat across template instances
- Custom chat IDs: Create shared discussion spaces with custom IDs

See interactiveGuideExample() for a comprehensive demonstration of these features.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/examples/slideshow_example.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/examples/slideshow_example/)

Exact arithmetic, smooth-transcendental tiers, and the 2D fBm palette have hard bounds; the 4D fbm4 hash comparison remains diagnostic because tiny differences in its warped coordinates can cross hash lattice boundaries. `uv saturate` must be bit-identical, which catches a flipped image.
